input: Steady-state conversion for an ideal continuous stirred-tank reactor (CSTR) running a hydrolysis that is first order in the limiting reactant is 84.9%. The rate constant at the operating temperature is 0.156 min-1, and the mean residence time in the vessel is 36 min. Conversion states the fraction of the limiting reactant that has reacted by the outlet, and a first-order reaction is one whose rate is proportional to the concentration of that reactant. Perfect mixing is assumed, so the composition and temperature are uniform through the vessel and the outlet stream has the vessel composition. Constant density is also assumed, so the mean residence time is set by the vessel volume and the volumetric flow alone. The estimate assumes perfect mixing and constant density; tracer tests on the actual vessel have not been run. The conversion figure therefore rests on the ideal-mixing assumption without an independent measurement of how long material actually spends in the vessel. A real vessel with short-circuiting or stagnant regions would hold a distribution of residence times rather than the single mean value, and its conversion would differ from the ideal figure in a direction the stated data do not fix. At its stated scope, the result is the conversion of the ideal reactor under the two named assumptions, not a measured performance of the installed vessel.
